aliases.name: Martini-Henry
aliases.note: The plain-hyphen spelling used interchangeably with the en dash form.

aliases.name: Aynalı Martin
aliases.note: The name used for the rifle in the Ottoman Empire, including in Ottoman-Turkish folk songs.

images.alt: Two views of a Martini-Henry rifle on a pale background, left and right sides, with a full wooden stock, a curved underlever ahead of the trigger guard, a flat steel receiver and a fixed rear sight ahead of the receiver
images.caption: A Martini-Henry Mark I of 1871 in the collections of the Swedish Army Museum. The underlever doubles as the trigger guard: pulling it down and forward tips the breech block clear of the chamber and draws back the striker spring in one motion.

images.alt: The disassembled falling-block action of a Martini-Henry Mark II laid out on a wooden bench: the breech block, hammerless striker and coil spring, the underlever, the tumbler and sear, and assorted pins
images.caption: The action of a Martini-Henry Mark II stripped to its parts, showing the block, striker and lever that together form the falling-block breech and its hammerless cocking mechanism.

images.alt: A re-enactor in Victorian British Army uniform and pith helmet firing a Martini-Henry rifle from a bench rest against a stone wall, smoke and muzzle flash visible at the muzzle
images.caption: A firing demonstration of a Martini-Henry rifle by a costumed re-enactor, showing the smoke and muzzle flash the black-powder cartridge produced.
